ORIGINAL NOT READ HERE -- the matwbn scan is behind an anti-bot gate; what follows is from Lagarias's own annotation in the annotated bibliography and from the 1985 survey. Terras proves that the integers with stopping time k form residue classes modulo 2^k up to finitely many elements (Theorem C of the survey) and that the set with finite stopping time has natural density one (Theorem A); the annotation credits him with exactly that and with introducing the coefficient stopping time, not with a rate. Terras 1979 supplies details of the density proof after Moeller's 1978 criticism. THE EXPONENTIAL RATE 2^(-eta k) FOR THE SURVIVORS IS THE SURVEY'S THEOREM D, built on Terras's structure theorem but stated and proved there -- see lagarias-1985-3x+1-problem. Nakanishi 2026 Remark 8 reads Terras as a central-limit argument that the ratio of unconverged parity vectors vanishes, which is again the density and not the rate.
title: A stopping time problem on the positive integers
